actions: pronates forearm (prime mover with wrist in neutral, deep to pronator teres' more proximal action)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Deepest forearm muscle, forming a flat quadrilateral sheet directly on the interosseous membrane between radius and ulna.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology
motor_endplate_zones.notes: An unusually long nerve-dense region spanning roughly half the muscle, about 3.41 cm2, entered from the deep upper edge by 3-5 primary branches of the anterior interosseous nerve. Highest spindle abundance in its middle third, at 58.93% of muscle length.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Zhou J, Jia F, Chen P, Zhou G, Wang M, Wu J, Yang S, 'Localisation of the centre of the highest region of muscle spindle abundance of anterior forearm muscles', J Anat 244(5):803-814 (2023), doi:10.1111/joa.14000 -- 24 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's staining with muscle-spindle histology and spiral CT localisation

injection_target_points.label: main
injection_target_points.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology, localised by spiral CT with barium sulphate labelling
injection_target_points.notes: The deepest target of the eight muscles, at 53.58% of limb thickness -- past halfway through the forearm. This is the point most likely to be the source's single posterior-surface projection, since pronator quadratus lies on the interosseous membrane, but the source does not say so in recoverable text and it is not asserted here. SURFACE NOT ESTABLISHED. The source places all but one of its eleven projection points on the anterior forearm and one on the posterior forearm, but the label identifying the exception was lost in full-text extraction, so `depth_measured_from` is omitted here rather than guessed. The three percentages are unaffected; confirm the surface against the paper's CT localisation figure before planning a needle path from the depth figure.
injection_target_points.source: Zhou J, Jia F, Chen P, Zhou G, Wang M, Wu J, Yang S, 'Localisation of the centre of the highest region of muscle spindle abundance of anterior forearm muscles', J Anat 244(5):803-814 (2023), doi:10.1111/joa.14000 -- 24 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's staining with muscle-spindle histology and spiral CT localisation

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the volar forearm, 3-4 cm proximal to the distal radioulnar joint.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deepest of the anterior compartment, lying directly on the radial and ulnar cortices and spanning between them.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Superficial and deep layers are separately resolvable, divided by an intramuscular fascia, with the interosseous membrane beneath.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Relaxing it removes resistance to supination and lets the biceps and supinator work, so it is often injected alongside pronator teres rather than instead of it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

trigger_points.location_description: Deep in the distal quarter of the volar forearm; direct palpation is limited and needling approaches are described from the ulnar side. The Trigger Point Manual 3rd edition includes pronator quadratus in the wrist-and-finger-flexor chapter.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Experimental intramuscular stimulation refers pain along the medial (ulnar) volar forearm, extending to the medial epicondyle and the 5th finger in 57% of subjects, or to the 3rd-4th fingers in 29%, resembling C8-T1 dermatomes and ulnar or median sensory patterns; deep ulnar-sided volar wrist ache mimicking ulnar neuropathy is the clinical translation.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Sustained pronated gripping (keyboard and mouse work, tool use), forearm fracture and immobilization. [clinical reasoning]
trigger_points.notes: Non-myofascial differential: DRUJ arthritis or instability, ulnar impaction, FCU tendinopathy, anterior interosseous nerve pathology, volar plate irritation, ulnar neuropathy, C8 radiculopathy.
trigger_points.source: Hwang, Kang & Kim (2005) Pain 116:238-242 (experimental referred-pain mapping); Donnelly et al. (2019) Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., ch. 38 (includes pronator quadratus in the wrist-and-finger-flexor chapter) -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference.

clinical.function_biomechanics: Major: The prime pronator: consistently active in pronation regardless of speed, load or elbow position, with PT recruited for fast or resisted pronation [57, 58, 60]. DRUJ stability: The deep head coapts the ulnar head into the sigmoid notch throughout rotation and is a dynamic stabilizer of the distal radioulnar joint, complementing the ECU subsheath and TFCC [37, 57, 58]. Wrist: No wrist crossing; its clinical output at the wrist is DRUJ control and deep distal volar forearm pain. Importance: Testing pronation with the elbow flexed isolates PQ from the humeral head of PT (anterior interosseous palsy); a pedicled PQ flap on the anterior interosseous vessels is used for coverage and vascularized bone transfer at the wrist [4, 43].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Bursae / sheaths: None. Relations: The deepest anterior muscle of the forearm; forms the floor beneath the FDP and FPL tendons; its distal edge lies at the watershed line of the distal radius, so it is elevated in the volar (Henry/FCR) approach and repaired or spared over volar plates as an FPL-protecting layer [4, 46]. Coupled structures: DRUJ and TFCC, interosseous membrane (distal oblique bundle region), FPL and FDP tendons, anterior interosseous nerve and artery [1, 37, 57].

trigger_points.location: Deep in the distal quarter of the volar forearm; direct palpation is limited and needling approaches are described from the ulnar side (the 3rd edition includes PQ in the wrist-and-finger-flexor chapter) [3].
trigger_points.referred_pain: Experimental intramuscular stimulation refers pain along the medial (ulnar) volar forearm, extending to the medial epicondyle and the 5th finger in 57% of subjects, or to the 3rd–4th fingers in 29%, resembling C8–T1 dermatomes and ulnar or median sensory patterns; deep ulnar-sided volar wrist ache mimicking ulnar neuropathy is the clinical translation [50].
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Sustained pronated gripping (keyboard and mouse work, tool use), forearm fracture and immobilization [clinical reasoning].

clinical.pain_referred_into_territory: Pain referred into PQ territory (deep distal volar forearm)
clinical.non_myofascial_differential: DRUJ arthritis or instability, ulnar impaction, FCU tendinopathy, anterior interosseous nerve pathology, volar plate irritation, ulnar neuropathy, C8 radiculopathy.
clinical.notes: In anterior interosseous nerve palsy (Kiloh–Nevin) PQ weakness is detected as loss of pronation strength with the elbow flexed [43]. Volar displacement of the pronator fat plane on the lateral radiograph is a soft-tissue sign of distal radius fracture [grade B] [4]. Whether PQ repair after volar plating improves outcome remains debated; its value as an FPL-protecting cover over the plate edge is the practical argument [4, 46].
clinical.caveat: Referred-pain maps from Travell and Simons are clinical consensus drawings, not experimentally derived; the APL and pronator quadratus maps (Hwang et al.) are experimental hypertonic-saline studies in healthy volunteers. Grade C items (Appendix A rows 23, 44–46, 48): TrP distances, muscle-level arterial detail, the ECRL/ECRB insertional bursa, the grip-strength claim for PL agenesis, and the extrapolated EDM/EPB/EPL referral statements. All are labelled in the text. Referred-pain conventions. "TrP referral" is the essential (dark) zone described by Travell and Simons unless "spillover" is stated. TrP locations in centimetres are approximations read from the Manual's figures and should be confirmed by palpation of the taut band. Quantitative biomechanical values are cadaveric means and vary with forearm rotation and wrist angle.
